'''Irina Veretennicoff''' is a [[physicist]], and [[professor emeritus]] of the [[Vrije Universiteit Brussel]]. Her major contributions to theoretical physics concern the interaction of light and matter, and [[photonics]].<ref name="kvab">{{cite web |title=KVAB: Irina Veretennicoff |url=https://kvab.be/nl/activiteiten/herlezingenreeks-irina-veretenicoff |access-date=2015-10-27 |publisher=kvab.be}}</ref>

== Career ==
Veretennicoff graduated in [[Physics]] from the [[Vrije Universiteit Brussel]] (VUB) in 1973 with a [[doctorate]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Irina Veretennicoff |url=https://kvab.be/sites/default/rest/?q=leden/id/1022&_=popup&width=768&height=720&iframe=true |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=kvab.be}}</ref> under the guidance of [[Radu Balescu]]<ref>{{cite web | title=Irina VERETENNICOFF &#124; Former head of Department Applied Physics and Photonics , now Emeritus &#124; PhD in Physics 1973. Supervisor: Prof Radu Balescu, Université Libre de Bruxelles, Group Ilya Prigogine &#124; Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Brussels &#124; VUB &#124; Applied Physics and Photonics , School of Engineering and Physics ,Faculty of Sciences &#124; Research profile | url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Irina-Veretennicoff }}</ref> of [[Université libre de Bruxelles]] (ULB).

Irina Veretennicoff has authored over 400 papers in theoretical physics<ref>{{Cite web |title=Irina Veretennicoff |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ePxBEsMAAAAJ |access-date=2024-07-13 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> and since 1988 has been an honorary member of the Class of Natural Sciences [[Royal Flemish Academy of Belgium for Science and the Arts]].<ref name=":0" />
